The main takeaway from our work is that

electroweak corrections to $W^\pm$ production at hadron machines are large, of the order of 10% for total cross sections and up to 50% for differential distributions, and that they are not negligible in precision measurements.

electroweak corrections beyond the $\mathcal{R}$-ratio are sizable for Tevatron and LHC kinematics, and they are important for a precise determination of the $W W$-gauge-boson couplings and for a test of the universality of the weak mixing angle.

the complete electroweak next-to-leading-order corrections can be safely ignored for most observables at the Tevatrons, whereas at the LHC they can be important, in particular for the total cross section and for the lepton transverse-momentum distribution.
